title: CTO Interview with Paweł Banachowicz of Silicon Creations
gist: Silicon Creations' Paweł Banachowicz describes how AI demand has pushed all markets to bleeding-edge nodes with compressed design cycles and often a single test chip, raising the premium on low-risk analog/mixed-signal clocking IP; the company (~200 staff, 500+ PLL products, 2,000+ chips at TSMC, 2nm in HVM) is focusing on DVFS and sub-nanosecond frequency switching, while noting foundry bans on feeding PDK data to AI limit AI-driven analog design.

insights.claim: Silicon Creations has almost 200 employees, more than 500 unique PLL products, over 2,000 chips taped out with its IP at TSMC, 2nm in high-volume mass production, and sub-2nm test chips taped out by customers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals deep entrenchment in the TSMC leading-edge ecosystem for clocking IP, relevant to IP-licensing competitive dynamics.
insights.locator: Soon I was tasked with designing

insights.claim: Silicon Creations' early work on a flagship PLL in TSMC's 16nm process using a super-early PDK for the first MPW in that node prepared it for the FinFET transition and became a turning point for the company.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Early-node access is a durable competitive advantage for IP vendors.
insights.locator: Soon I was tasked with designing

themes.theme: Compressed design cycles and rising failure costs

insights.claim: Chip design cycles have shrunk: where five years from idea to mass production was typical and HPC, automotive, industrial and aerospace followed mobile SoCs into new nodes years later, all markets now compete at or near bleeding-edge processes without waiting for maturity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Broader, faster leading-edge node adoption supports demand for advanced foundry capacity and proven IP.
insights.quote: Now all markets compete at or near bleeding-edge processes, without waiting for maturity.

insights.claim: AI computational demand across mobile, automotive, HPC and even IoT is driving the rush to latest nodes, and companies often make only one test chip before going to production, with chiplets mitigating yield issues in large monolithic designs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Fewer test chips raise the value of de-risked silicon-proven IP and increase cost of any failure.
insights.quote: companies often make only one test chip before going to production

insights.claim: The cost of chip failure is now at an unimaginable level, so customers need low-risk, predictable analog and mixed-signal foundations to meet aggressive schedules.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Supports pricing power for proven IP vendors versus cheaper but riskier alternatives.
insights.quote: The cost of failure was always high, but now it is on an unimaginable level.
insights.locator: The cost of failure was always high

insights.claim: Banachowicz argues headline PLL performance from academic papers is achieved in narrow conditions, and the commonly used integrated phase jitter figure of merit from 12kHz to 20MHz, defined for SONET networks, may no longer have practical meaning.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Benchmarks used in IP selection may mislead; real-world robustness is the differentiator.
insights.quote: But the Figure of Merit being optimized may no longer have practical meaning.
insights.locator: What other approaches are being used

insights.claim: Silicon Creations verifies its IP at extreme PVT conditions including mismatch and lifetime device degradation, and conservatively accounts for unmodeled effects known from years of silicon experience.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains the vendor's de-risking value proposition in a single-test-chip world.

themes.theme: Power management roadmap: DVFS and fast clocking

insights.claim: Silicon Creations is investing heavily in DVFS, building sensing and actuation IP that detects voltage movements, temperature, latency and device degradation and regulates the clock to maintain performance and mitigate supply dips or thermal runaway, because performance per watt drives the industry.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Power efficiency is the key AI-chip constraint; on-die sensing/clocking IP is a growing content opportunity.
insights.quote: Performance per watt drives the industry.
insights.locator: What challenges will your customers face

insights.claim: Silicon Creations has a line of IPs that can change clock frequency from almost any frequency to another in under a nanosecond without multiple clock sources.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Fast frequency switching enables more aggressive power management in AI accelerators.

themes.theme: AI's impact on the IP business and its limits

insights.claim: AI accelerated Silicon Creations' business: existing customers launched new projects while new customers suddenly began developing dozens of AI chips in parallel.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Proliferation of AI chip startups and projects drives demand for licensed clocking/SerDes IP.
insights.quote: customers that didn’t exist yesterday suddenly began developing dozens of AI chips in parallel

insights.claim: Foundries have forbidden feeding PDK-related data to AI, including on-premises agents, and IP vendors cannot train LLMs on customer data, limiting AI use in analog design.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Foundry data restrictions constrain AI-driven analog design tools; a headwind for EDA-AI claims in analog.
insights.quote: Foundries have forbidden feeding PDK-related data to AI, including on-premises agents.
insights.locator: But not everything is that beautiful.

insights.claim: Banachowicz dismisses the idea of handing DRM and SPICE models to an agent to design a chip, while noting digital teams have more AI freedom because HDL is technology agnostic and can integrate controllers like DisplayPort, Ethernet and PCIe in days rather than months.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI productivity gains in chip design skew to digital over analog; analog IP expertise stays scarce.
insights.quote: Forget about handing DRM and SPICE models to an agent and asking it to design a chip.
insights.locator: Forget about handing DRM and SPICE
